title: Best Pressure Washing Business Software (2026 Prices)
description: Jobber vs Housecall Pro vs Workiz vs ResponsiBid for pressure washing: quoting, upsells, seasonal pauses, users and real published prices, checked Oct 2026.
h1: Best pressure washing business software for small crews
body:
Pressure washing and soft washing jobs are won on speed: a homeowner asks for a driveway, house wash or roof price, and the first clear quote with add-ons (sealing, gutter brightening, a back patio) usually gets the job. After that you need scheduling that survives rain delays, and a way to take payment before you leave the property. Below are the tools we could verify for pressure washing businesses from the vendors' own pages, checked 2026-10-23.

{{table:jobber,housecall-pro,workiz,responsibid}}

1. Jobber: lowest published price for a full system

Jobber Core is $29/mo billed annually or $49/mo with no commitment, for 1 user. Annual sign-ups before Oct 30, 2026 get a promotional $21/mo for the first 12 months. Extra users are $29/mo each. Jobber's pressure washing page lists request forms for your website, Google Business Profile or a QR code on your truck, quotes with photos, saved quote templates for driveway, roof soft wash, deck/fence and house wash jobs, bulk rescheduling for weather delays, and job costing that tracks labor and chemical spend. Two things matter for pressure washers: optional line items (upsells) on quotes start on Grow ($149/mo billed annually, $199/mo monthly), and automated quote follow-ups, automatic payments and QuickBooks Online sync start on Connect ($99/mo annually, $139/mo monthly). Online card payments are 2.9% + 30¢, Tap to Pay is 2.7% + 30¢, and ACH is 1%. The trial is 14 days on Grow with no credit card. {{aff:jobber|See Jobber plans}}

2. Housecall Pro: multi-option estimates and users included

Housecall Pro Basic is $59/mo billed annually ($79/mo monthly) for 1 user and includes online booking, estimates and invoicing, consumer financing, a price book and job costing. Its pressure washing page describes multi-option estimates for pressure washing, soft washing, sealing and add-ons, deposits on estimates, digital signatures, rain-delay rescheduling and before-and-after photos saved to the job. Essentials ($149/mo annually, $189/mo monthly) includes 5 users and adds routes, flat-rate pricing, checklists, photo reports, employee GPS tracking and QuickBooks Online sync. MAX ($299/mo annually, $329/mo monthly) includes 8 users ($35/mo per extra user) and adds recurring service plans, route optimization and a sales proposal tool. Card processing starts at 2.59% and bank payments are 1%. No long-term contract; the 14-day MAX trial needs no credit card. {{aff:housecallpro|See Housecall Pro plans}}

3. Workiz: phone system built in, but no public prices

Workiz has a dedicated pressure washing page and three plans (Standard, Pro, Ultimate), but its pricing page shows "Request pricing" instead of prices, so the cost is unknown until you talk to sales. Every plan lists scheduling, estimates and invoices, online booking with optional checkout, estimate deposits, tap to pay, consumer financing, recurring jobs, QuickBooks Online sync and an integrated phone system. The Good/Better/Best sales proposals and service plans that its pressure washing page highlights are Ultimate-only features, and so are Zapier and the open API. Genius Scheduling is on Pro and Ultimate. Workiz lists a 7-day free trial with no credit card and says annual billing saves "$400+". Card processing rates aren't published, and card readers are sold separately. Workiz pricing page

4. ResponsiBid: instant quotes on your website

ResponsiBid isn't a full CRM. It's a quoting and sales tool, and pressure washing is one of the industries it names as a best fit. The Startup plan is free (quoting calculator, multiple service tiers, auto-upsell, sales pipeline). Scaling ($179/mo) adds instant quoting on your own website, follow-up email, unlimited sub-users, and connections to Jobber, Housecall Pro, ServiceMonster, Markate, The Customer Factor or Google Calendar so quoted work lands on your schedule. Pro ($229/mo) adds bundles, text follow-up, CrewCal scheduling intelligence, customer self-scheduling, deposits, Zapier and review invites. There's a one-time setup fee (the amount isn't published), no long-term contract, and a $50/mo seasonal pause for up to 4 months a year on monthly plans, which matters if you shut down for winter. See our ResponsiBid pricing details.

Which should you pick?

  • Solo operator, just starting: Jobber Core has the lowest published price for quoting, scheduling, invoicing and payments in one app. Upsell line items need Grow, though, so add that cost to your math if you sell add-ons.
  • Two trucks or a small crew: Housecall Pro Essentials includes 5 users for $149/mo billed annually. Jobber's 5-user Connect tier is also listed at $149/mo billed annually, but Jobber's upsell line items need Grow, whose 5-user tier is listed at $229/mo billed annually.
  • Lots of web leads asking "how much?": add ResponsiBid Scaling or Pro on top of Jobber or Housecall Pro so homeowners can price a driveway or house wash on your site.
  • Seasonal businesses: Jobber's monthly no-commitment billing can be cancelled any time, Housecall Pro has no long-term contract, and ResponsiBid has the $50/mo seasonal pause. Jobber's annual prepaid plans aren't refundable mid-term.
  • Workiz: only worth a demo if you want its built-in phone system and Ultimate features. Without published prices we can't compare its cost.

faq: What is the cheapest pressure washing business software?

Of the tools we checked on 2026-10-23, ResponsiBid's Startup quoting plan is free. The cheapest full CRM with published pricing is Jobber Core at $29/mo billed annually ($49/mo with no commitment), with a $21/mo first-year promo for annual sign-ups before Oct 30, 2026. Workiz doesn't publish prices.
Which pressure washing software lets me upsell add-ons on a quote?

Jobber lists optional line items on its Grow plan and up. Housecall Pro's pressure washing page lists multi-option estimates for add-on services. Workiz lists Good/Better/Best sales proposals on Ultimate. ResponsiBid includes auto-upsell and multiple service tiers on every plan, including the free Startup plan.

Workiz doesn't publish prices. Its pricing page shows 'Request pricing' for the Standard, Pro and Ultimate plans as of 2026-10-23. It lists a 7-day free trial with no credit card and says annual billing saves $400+.
Can I pause pressure washing software in the winter?

ResponsiBid offers a seasonal pause at $50/mo for up to 4 months a year on monthly plans. Jobber's monthly no-commitment plan can be cancelled at any time, and Housecall Pro says it has no long-term contracts. We found no seasonal pause published by Jobber, Housecall Pro or Workiz.
Do these tools sync with QuickBooks?

Jobber syncs with QuickBooks Online and Xero on Connect and up. Housecall Pro syncs with QuickBooks Online on Essentials and up. Workiz lists QuickBooks Online sync on all plans. ResponsiBid doesn't list QuickBooks on its pricing page and relies on the CRM it connects to.
